# Agatha Sowerby

## Overview

- **Age:** Stout, elderly woman  <sub>[v1 c9 P30](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0030), [v1 c10 P34](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0034)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000)</sub>
- **Status:** Widowed  <sub>[v2 c26 P2](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0002)</sub>
- **Origin:** Brierley  <sub>[v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000), [v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001)</sub>
- **Role:** Homemaker and community organizer  <sub>[v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001)</sub>
- **Titles:** Mrs. Agatha Sowerby  <sub>[v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000)</sub>; Mrs. Agatha  <sub>[v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000)</sub>; Agatha  <sub>[v1 c1 P11](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0011)</sub>

## Appearance

Agatha Sowerby is a stout, heavy woman who walks with a waddle. She has a sharp, perceptive gaze, a forceful manner of speaking, and a energetic, busy presence.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v1 c9 P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014), [v1 c9 P30](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0030), [v1 c10 P34](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0034), [v2 c6 P57](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0057)_

## Personality

Agatha is an extraordinarily industrious, observant, and capable woman who manages her household efficiently while taking a vigilant interest in the affairs of her neighbors. She prides herself on always expressing her mind freely and candidly, regardless of how blunt her opinions may sound. Though she can be pessimistic, stern, and overly inquisitive, she possesses a kindly, sympathetic heart and a strong commitment to community work and helping those in need.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000), [v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v1 c1 P24](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0024), [v1 c1 P28](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0028), [v1 c9 P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014), [v1 c10 P33](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0033), [v1 c10 P38](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0038), [v2 c7 P31](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0031)_

## History

Agatha Sowerby kept a watchful eye over all travelers entering or leaving Brierley from her kitchen window in Sowerby’s Hollow. In June, she observed Obed Abernethy dressed in his finest clothes and buggy, leading her to visit Thirza Abernethy at Grey Shutters, where she learned they were adopting an orphanage boy. When Obed brought home a red-haired girl named Nell Harcourt by mistake, Agatha voiced strong disapproval and misgivings. After suffering a severe bout of influenza, she visited Grey Shutters to inspect Nell, criticizing her freckles and red hair, which provoked Nell into a fiery rage. After Nell was disciplined, she offered a dramatic apology that completely won Agatha over. Over the following years, Agatha remained a central figure in Brierley’s community affairs, leading the Church Aid Society and evaluating new ministers, schoolteachers, and neighbors. When her husband Thomas fell ill, she cared for him devotedly until his quiet death. Following his passing, the farm was sold to pay a mortgage, and Agatha accepted Thirza’s invitation to move into Grey Shutters, establishing her own quarters in the former spare room and bringing her industrious nature and advice to the household.

## Background by volume

- Raised ten sons and daughters, and buried two children  <sub>[v1 c9 P30](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0030)</sub>
- Lived in a home situated at the road slope in Sowerby's Hollow  <sub>[v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000)</sub>
- Directed the Sewing Circle, assisted in Sunday school, and led the Church Aid Society and Foreign Missions Auxiliary  <sub>[v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001)</sub>
- Knitted sixteen cotton warp quilts, highly respected by local homemakers  <sub>[v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001)</sub>
- Her husband's Boston employer once defrauded him of ten dollars, creating her lifelong bias against Americans  <sub>[v2 c1 P49](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0049)</sub>

## Quotes

> Following tea, I will simply pop over to Grey Shutters and ascertain from Thirza his destination and reasoning.  <sub>[v1 c1 P5](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0005)</sub>
